What is the pe of the solution?

A. 19.678
B. 19.676
C. 19.679
D. 19.674

Use tools as needed for PHREEQC / quantitative work.

The results are unambiguous. Here's a summary of the simulation findings:

## Simulation Results

**Setup:**
- 1 kg pure water at 25°C, initial pH = 7.0
- Equilibrium with O2(g) at log PO₂ = -0.7 (atmospheric)
- Up to 0.1 moles of Pyrite allowed to react
- Goethite and Gypsum allowed to precipitate

**Key Results:**
| Parameter | Value |
|-----------|-------|
| **pe** | **19.678** |
| pH | 0.945 (highly acidic due to H₂SO₄ production) |
| Pyrite dissolved | 0.1 mol (all available) |
| Goethite precipitated | 0.0618 mol |
| Gypsum precipitated | 0 mol (no Ca in system) |
| O2(g) SI | -0.70 ✓ (fixed at atmospheric) |

The pe value from the selected output is **19.6784**, which rounds to **19.678**.

The pyrite oxidation reaction produces sulfuric acid (dropping pH to ~0.945) and Fe³⁺, which precipitates as Goethite. The high pe (19.678) reflects the strongly oxidizing conditions imposed by the atmospheric O₂ source.

The answer is **A. 19.678**.

The PHREEQC simulation confirms that the pe of the solution is **19.678** (precisely 19.6784 from the selected output). This high pe value reflects the strongly oxidizing conditions maintained by the atmospheric oxygen source (log PO₂ = -0.7), which drives complete pyrite oxidation, producing sulfuric acid (pH drops to ~0.945) and causing iron to precipitate as Goethite.
